paragraphs: Friend, here's what this whole passage is shouting at us: Jesus is both willing and able. A man with leprosy kneels and says, "Lord, if You are willing, You can make me clean." Jesus reaches out His hand, touches him, and says, "I am willing." (Matthew 8:2-3) So when you wonder whether Jesus cares about what you're carrying, start right there.

Now look at the centurion, an army officer. He says, "just say the word, and my servant will be healed," and Jesus marvels at his faith. (Matthew 8:8, 10) He trusted that a word from Jesus was enough, with no show and no touch required. And then Jesus says, "As you have believed, so will it be done for you." (Matthew 8:13) Baker, that is an invitation to trust what Jesus says even when you can't see how it's going to work out yet.

Then Matthew pulls the curtain back with Isaiah: "He took up our infirmities and carried our diseases." (Matthew 8:17) Jesus didn't heal from a safe distance. He stepped into our mess and carried it. Friend, I sat in a drawer for years thinking nobody was coming, and I'm telling you, somebody came. Trust Him with whatever you're carrying today, because He is willing, and He is able.
